title: The Two Hosts in the Senses: Seals and Archons in the Daily Working of the Body
arc: Hidden in the senses of the human body two great hosts are at work — the divine seals and the archons of darkness; the teaching describes how, daily, the chosen are purified inward toward the Father while the archons of darkness are driven outward into Error, with some still concealed and awaiting separation.
reading:
Although heavily damaged, this teaching opens a window onto a very specific Manichaean-correspondential subject: the hidden cosmology of the senses themselves. Its claim is that the body of the human being — and especially its receptive faculties, the seven gates — is not a neutral organ but a populated battlefield in which two ordered hosts operate continuously upon every act of perception.

The teaching first asserts that "powers" dwell in this organ, with their own root and their own existence, working "daily, unto the body of the man." This is the standard correspondential principle that the natural body, far from being inert, is a field through which spiritual influxes constantly pass. The senses are gates, and the gates are governed by powers that are themselves rooted in the higher and lower worlds.

The teaching then states the count of these powers in two parallel inventories. There are two hundred thousand seals in it, and there are also twenty myriads of archons. The number is the same on both sides: the imprint of confirmed correspondence — the seals by which the Lord fixes truth in the soul — is met member-for-member by an opposing host of archons belonging to the Darkness. Every receptive point in the natural where the divine can stamp its likeness is also a point where a falsity-from-evil stands ready to take hold. The senses are thus an exact mirror of the cosmic war: light-seals against dark archons, evenly arrayed in the body's gates.

The middle of the teaching describes what happens to these two hosts. Of the seals (or of the souls and truths bound up with them) it is said: "they are chosen, and they are purified, and they come inward." This is the threefold regenerative motion — election, purification, inward gathering — by which divine truth is refined out of the mingled state and conveyed upward through the discrete degrees. The medium of this inward motion is named in fragments: it happens "in the voice, in the speech … habitually," and it is associated with stillness — "stillness with the Stillness, at the time when his heart …" The senses, which on the surface only see and hear, are revealed as inner organs of the Call and the Hearing: through voice and speech the Father's summons reaches the heart, and in stillness the heart answers, so that the chosen are gathered inward "of God the Father."

Against this inward motion stands the opposite motion described next. The twelve — the full zodiacal completeness of states — together with the myriads of archons "that belong to the Darkness" are habitually driven away "to the outside, in the Error, in the meta…rhismos." Where the seals move inward toward the Father, the archons move outward into Error, the cosmic principle of deception. This is the discrimination of regeneration in its second face: separation forth. The same daily work that gathers the chosen inward also expels the archons of darkness outward, refusing them entry into the inner organism. The senses become a sieve, sorting at every moment what may be conveyed upward into the Mind of Light and what must be cast out into the wandering of Error.

The teaching closes by acknowledging that this sorting is not yet complete. "There are some among them … there are others among them whom they habitually conceal." Some powers in the senses are still hidden — neither yet purified inward nor yet driven outward. This is the honest realism of the teaching: in the present mingled state of the cosmos, every human sensory life contains a residue that has not yet declared itself, falsities still under cover and truths not yet awakened. The work of judgment, of separating forth, continues daily in the watch-stations of the body until what is chosen is wholly gathered to the Father and what is dark is wholly fixed outside in Error.

Read as a whole, then, the teaching is a doctrine of the senses as a cosmic battlefield in miniature. The body is a temple inhabited by two hundred thousand seals and twenty myriads of archons; voice, speech, and stillness are its inner liturgy; election, purification, and inward gathering are its daily regenerative work; expulsion into Error is its complementary act of separation; and concealment is the residue still awaiting the final judgment. The senses are not merely organs of perception — they are the daily working-place where the cosmic war between Light and Darkness is fought out in each individual human form.
